formation.title: The Most Serene Republic of Saint George
formation.text:
For a century and more the Casa di San Giorgio has kept Genoa's taxes, struck its coin and governed its colonies, while the Doge kept the title. Now the Protectors sit in the Palazzo as the city's masters. Machiavelli wrote that the Casa showed liberty and tyranny within the same community, and that if it took the whole city Genoa would be a republic more memorable than Venice. The Great Council must decide what that republic is to be: a state that governs the Riviera, Corsica and the colonies through its own governors, or a bank that keeps a city as its seat and lends to the kings of Europe.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

modifiers.name: The Protectors Rule
modifiers.text: The Casa governs its lands as a state, through its own governors and garrisons.

options.text: The Casa remains a bank first

modifiers.name: Lender of Kings
modifiers.text: The Republic is the bank's seat; its business is the purses of crowns.

advances.name: The Great Council of San Giorgio
advances.text: Four hundred and eighty shareholders sit in the Great Council and choose the eight Protectors, half by ballot and half by lot. The Republic's creditors are its legislators, and they vote their dividend with the state in mind.

advances.name: Money of the Bank
advances.text: Deposits in the Casa's cartulari pass from one account to another as money of the bank. A depositor who can pay with a line in the ledger has less reason to run for coin.

advances.name: The Darsena
advances.text: Genoa's walled dock and arsenal by the old port, where the Republic's galleys winter and are built.

advances.name: The Mint of San Giorgio
advances.text: By 1437 the Casa runs the Commune's mint as well as its taxes, and the city's coin comes from the bank.

advances.name: The Governors of Corsica
advances.text: In 1453 the island's assembly asked the Casa to govern Corsica. It rules through its own governor and the old councils of Cismonte and Pumonte.

event.title: The Corsican Revolt
event.text: In 1729 the villagers of Bustanico refused a tax collector, and the island rose behind them. Our garrisons hold Bastia and the coast; the interior belongs to the rebels' councils. The Emperor offers troops and a settlement on the island's terms: pardon, restored councils and lighter taxes. Others in the Senate want the revolt crushed and the tax collected.

modifiers.name: The Treaty of Corte
modifiers.text: Corsica's councils and pardons restored on the island's terms.

options.text: Garrison the island and collect the tax

modifiers.name: Garrisons of Corsica
modifiers.text: Our garrisons hold the island and collect its tax.

advances.name: Caffa and Gazaria
advances.text: In 1453 the Doge ceded Caffa and the Black Sea colonies to the Casa for ever. The bank collects their taxes and keeps their consuls.

advances.name: Counters Open to All
advances.text: The Casa takes deposits from anyone who brings them, and the city's savings stand behind its loans.

advances.name: Velvet of Genoa
advances.text: Cut and figured velvet, silk on silk, woven in the city's looms from Levantine and Calabrian silk: the cloth every court of Europe calls Genoese.

advances.name: The Asientos of Spain
advances.text: Short loans to the crown of Spain, paid out in Flanders or Milan and secured by juros the banker may sell if the king does not pay. In the age of the Genoese two of every three of Philip II's loans were ours.

event.title: The Suspension of Payments
event.text: On 1 September 1575, three weeks after the silver fleet came in, the King of Spain suspended every payment on his debts: twelve million ducats of interest and principal, nearly two years of his revenue. Our houses hold seven parts in ten of it. The other bankers are forming a front and refusing the crown another ducat until it settles; the King's ministers ask us to keep the money flowing to his armies in Flanders.

options.text: Hold with the bankers until the King settles

modifiers.name: The Bankers' Front
modifiers.text: We held with the other bankers until the crown settled in juros.

modifiers.name: Lent Through the Storm
modifiers.text: We kept the King's armies paid while every other bank refused.

advances.name: The Fairs of Bisenzone
advances.text: Four times a year the Genoese bankers meet at the exchange fair, at Besancon and later Piacenza, and settle the bills of half of Europe without moving a coin.

event.title: The Fairs of Bisenzone
event.text: Shut out of Lyon, the Genoese bankers hold their own exchange fair under the Emperor's protection, at Besancon and later Piacenza. Four times a year a few dozen bankers meet for a week, clear the bills of exchange of half of Europe against each other, and fix the rates at which the King of Spain's money moves from Seville to Antwerp. Little coin changes hands; the ledgers do the work.

options.text: The fair sets the rate of Europe

advances.name: Galleys of the Asiento
advances.text: Since Andrea Doria took his galleys to the Emperor in 1528, the Republic's captains have served Spain under contract: the fleet is a business like any loan.

advances.name: The Corsican Companies
advances.text: The Casa fought the island's barons with Corsican men, and the Republic paid Corsican companies against Sampiero. Hill soldiers who know every path of the maquis.

advances.name: The New Walls
advances.text: After the Savoyard invasion of 1625 the Republic raised nineteen kilometres of bastioned wall over the ridges behind the city, the Mura Nuove, finished in 1639.

event.title: The New Walls
event.text: In 1625 the Duke of Savoy marched to the walls of the city with French help, and only Spanish galleys saved it. The Republic answers in stone: nineteen kilometres of bastioned wall along the ridges behind Genoa, enclosing the hills from which an army could look down into the port. The Mura Nuove are finished in 1639.

options.text: No army will look down on the port again

advances.name: The Albergo dei Poveri
advances.text: Emanuele Brignole's great poorhouse on the hill of Carbonara, founded in 1652 and endowed by the city's families, houses and feeds the poor and keeps the city quiet.

advances.name: The Cretan Loans
advances.text: From 1645 to 1669 Genoese capital financed Venice's long war for Crete. The old rival's war, paid for by the bank.

advances.name: The Porto Franco
advances.text: From 1590 foreign ships may trade in the port of Genoa free of duty, and the free port is widened through the next century.

advances.name: The Militia of Portoria
advances.text: In December 1746 the artisans and porters of Portoria drove an Austrian army out of the city in five days. The quarters keep their arms.

event.title: Che l'inse?
event.text: On 5 December 1746 an Austrian gun carriage sank into the mud of Portoria, and the soldiers ordered the townsfolk to haul it out. A boy picked up a stone and asked, in Genoese, whether he should start. In five days the artisans and porters of the quarters drove the Austrian army out of the city, while the patricians watched from their palaces. The people of Genoa have learned they can defend it.

advances.name: The Accademia Ligustica
advances.text: Founded in 1751 by the city's patricians, the academy teaches painting, sculpture and architecture to the Republic's artists.

advances.name: The Notes of the Cartulari
advances.text: Receipts of the Casa's ledgers pass from hand to hand as money, and the bank lends on them at its own rate.

advances.name: The Neutral Emporium
advances.text: The Republic keeps out of the century's wars and sells to every side.

destiny.name: The Casa Takes the City
destiny.text:
For a century the Casa's compere collected Genoa's taxes as its creditors. Now they collect them as the state.

Requires stability of 25 or more.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Casa Takes the City
event.text: The Protectors now sit in the Doge's palace as well as their own. The gabelles on salt, wine and grain that the compere farmed for a century are the Republic's revenues, and its collectors are the state's.

options.text: The ledgers and the state are one

destiny.name: The Maona Restored
destiny.text: In 1347 the Commune's creditors took Chios and Phocaea in place of payment, and their company ruled the island until 1566. Hold Chios and Phocaea, ourselves or through a protectorate, and keep 1,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: The Protectors govern a state
Own Chíos, or a subject owns it
Own Foça, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Maona Restored
event.text: Chios and its mastic, Phocaea and its alum are ours again, as they were the Maona's when the Commune's creditors took them in 1347. The Giustiniani's heirs ask to keep the island's revenues as a company; the Protectors remember how such companies end.

options.text: The islands answer to the Palazzo

destiny.name: Gazaria
destiny.text: In 1453 the Doge gave the Black Sea colonies to the Casa as the only power able to defend them. Hold Caffa and Tana, ourselves or through a protectorate, keep three protectorates, and stand at 50 prestige.

conditions.text: Own Kaffa, or a subject owns it
Own Tana, or a subject owns it
We have three protectorates or more
Prestige at least 50

event.title: Gazaria Again
event.text: Caffa and Tana fly the cross of Saint George again. In 1453 the Casa took the Black Sea colonies because no one else could defend them, and lost them twenty-two years later. This time the colonies must either pay their way in tribute from the caravans or be garrisoned to hold.

options.text: Let the caravans pay for Gazaria

modifiers.name: Tribute of the Caravans
modifiers.text: Gazaria pays its way from the caravan trade.

modifiers.name: Garrisons of Gazaria
modifiers.text: Caffa and Tana are held by the Republic's garrisons.

destiny.name: The Republic of Many Seas
destiny.text: Famagusta, ceded to the Casa in 1447, and Tabarka, the Lomellini's coral island off Tunis. Hold both, ourselves or through a protectorate, stand at 75 prestige and keep 3,000 gold.

conditions.text: Own Famagusta, or a subject owns it
Own Tabarka, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Republic of Many Seas
event.text: From Tabarka to Famagusta, from Chios to Caffa, the Republic's governors and protectorates hold the ports the Genoese held at their height. The Great Council must decide how to rule them: as a navy's bases or as communities with their own councils.

options.text: An admiralty for the many seas

modifiers.name: Admiralty of the Many Seas
modifiers.text: The Republic rules its distant ports as a navy's bases.

modifiers.name: Councils of the Colonies
modifiers.text: Every colony keeps its own council under the Republic.

destiny.name: Banker to Two Courts
destiny.text: The Spinola, Grimaldi and Centurione sat at more than one court at once. Sit as court banker to two crowns and keep 1,000 gold.

conditions.text: The Casa remains a bank first
We sit as court banker to two crowns or more
Gold at least 1000

event.title: Banker to Two Courts
event.text: Two crowns now keep our men at their courts and take our money on our terms. The Casa's ledgers record the revenues of kingdoms as once they recorded the salt tax of Genoa.

destiny.name: The Purse of Kings
destiny.text: Be master of the purse of two crowns, keep offices in Lisbon and Naples, and keep 2,000 gold.

conditions.text: We are master of the purse of two crowns or more
We keep offices in Lisbon and Naples
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Purse of Kings
event.text: Two kings cannot pay a regiment without our consent, and our offices stand in Lisbon and Naples. Philip II's bankers learned that a king who cannot pay pays in juros, bonds on his taxes; the Pallavicino learned that a Genoese house may lend to the heretic queen as well. The Protectors must choose how far the Republic's purse will reach.

modifiers.name: Juros of Castile
modifiers.text: The Republic's capital is bound up in the King's bonds.

modifiers.name: Lender to Every Side
modifiers.text: The Republic's houses lend to Catholic and heretic alike.

destiny.name: The Banker of Europe
destiny.text: Sit as court banker to four crowns, hold the purse of Castile or Spain, keep 3,000 gold and stand at 75 prestige. We may build the Casa delle Compere in our capital.

conditions.text: We sit as court banker to four crowns or more
We are master of the purse of Castile or Spain
Gold at least 3000
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Banker of Europe
event.text: Four crowns keep the Republic's men at court and Spain's purse is in our hands. Machiavelli's republic more memorable than Venice is not a republic of soldiers but of ledgers, and the Casa delle Compere registers the debts of a continent.

modifiers.name: Protectors of Europe's Credit
modifiers.text: The credit of Europe passes through the Republic's hands.

modifiers.name: Patrons of Genoa
modifiers.text: The fortunes made abroad are spent at home.

units.name: Galley of the Asiento
units.text: A galley built and crewed under contract, slower than a raider but fit for long blockades.

units.name: Corsican Companies
units.text: Light hill infantry raised from the Corsican villages.

units.name: Militia of Portoria
units.text: The armed artisans and porters of the Republic's towns.

buildings.name: Exchange Bank of the Fairs
buildings.text: Where the Republic's bankers discount the bills of the exchange fairs. In the capital it adds to the bank's loan capacity.

effect_groups.label: To the country, when built in the capital

buildings.name: Velvet Looms
buildings.text: Genoese weavers cutting and figuring velvet from silk.

buildings.name: The New Walls
buildings.text: Bastioned walls over the ridges behind the capital.

buildings.name: Albergo dei Poveri
buildings.text: A great poorhouse that houses and feeds the town's poor.

buildings.name: Accademia Ligustica
buildings.text: An academy of painting, sculpture and architecture.

effect_groups.label: To the country, when built in the capital

buildings.name: The Darsena
buildings.text: A walled dock and arsenal for building and repairing ships.

buildings.name: Casa delle Compere
buildings.text: The hall of the Casa's funds, where the debts of a continent are registered. In the capital, crowns answer us better and our pledges pay more.

effect_groups.label: To the country, when built in the capital

list.name: Office of the Protectors
list.text: The eight Protectors of San Giorgio, chosen by the Great Council of shareholders, keep the Casa's funds and answer for its credit. While they are paid and watched, depositors trust the books; left alone, their dealings come to light.

list.name: Office of Corsica
list.text: From 1453 the Casa governed Corsica through its own governor and the island's councils of Cismonte and Pumonte. The office now oversees all the Republic's protectorates: their tribute, their councils and their loyalty.

conditions.text: We hold a protectorate

list.name: Compere of the Salt
list.text: Every fund of the Casa was repaid by a named tax, and the salt gabelle was the oldest. The office farms the Republic's taxes to its creditors: well kept, the gabelles come in in full; neglected, the farmers keep what they collect.

list.name: Magistracy of the Galleys
list.text: The magistrates who built the Republic's galleys in the Darsena, manned their oars and hired them to Spain under contract. Neglected, the galleys rot at their moorings.

conditions.text: The capital
